title: Shaving the hair
hookLine: a baby's first hair, weighed, and its weight in silver given away

lines: THE HAIR HE WAS BORN WITH.
cards: A grandson has been born. His name is al-Hasan, and his mother is Fatimah, the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. The baby can't hold anything, can't say anything, can't do a single thing for anyone.
And the Prophet gives his daughter an instruction about the softest, lightest thing the baby has: the hair he was born with. Not to keep it. Not to throw it away.

teach.h: SHAVE IT. WEIGH IT. GIVE ITS WEIGHT.
teach.b: Here's the report, in Jami' at-Tirmidhi, in paraphrase. When al-Hasan was born, the Prophet said to Fatimah: shave his head, and give the weight of his hair in silver as charity.

teach.h: A DIRHAM, OR PART OF ONE.
teach.b: So they weighed it, the report says, and it came to a dirham, or part of a dirham. A coin, maybe less. The amount is small, and the hadith says so plainly.
The point isn't the size of the gift. Something taken from the child becomes something given in the child's name. Second, the half-sentence left over from yesterday.

The hadith in Bukhari said: shed blood on the child's behalf, and remove harm from him. What harm? The hadith doesn't say, and some readers take it to mean this very thing: the hair the baby was born with.
And a hadith in Sunan Abu Dawud, in paraphrase, sets the seventh day in one line: the 'aqiqah sacrificed, the head shaved, the child named. Third, what families do now.

Some still shave the baby's head on the seventh day and weigh the hair. Others estimate the weight and give its value in money. Scholars discuss the details, and families follow the school and the custom they know.
Fourth, look at it from the baby's side. A baby owns nothing, can't earn, can't even hold a coin. And yet, on day seven, there's already charity written in the baby's name.
Before a child can do a single good deed, the family does one for them.

teach.h: A BABY ARRIVES AS A GIVER.
teach.b: The child arrives in the world as a giver.

how: On or around the seventh day, some Muslim families shave the newborn's head and give the weight of the hair in silver, or its value in money, to charity, alongside the 'aqiqah and the naming.

o: a boy's first haircut, kept as a keepsake for the family

games.q: you're Fatimah. your son al-Hasan is a week old, and the Prophet tells you to shave his head. what happens to the hair?
o: weigh it, and give its weight in silver as charity.
save it for his wedding day.
games.why: they weighed it, and it came to a dirham or part of one, given as charity: a gift in the baby's name.

practice: Bring one child to mind: your own, a niece, a neighbor's new baby, or the child you once were, and say their name quietly.
Think of something small that could be given in that name, a coin in a box or a meal for someone; the hadith's amount wasn't large either.
If you pray, ask good for that child in your own words; if not, just hold their name and the gift together.

wordCard.voice: Shaving the hair. On the seventh day, a baby's first hair is shaved, and its weight in silver is given away in charity. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: shaving, as of the head.

carryVoice: Your line: weight in silver. Something light, given in a name that can't give yet. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1519 (al-Hasan's hair weighed; its weight in silver given; a dirham or part of a dirham)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5471–5472 (shed blood for him, and remove harm from him)
Sunan Abu Dawud 2838 (every child is in pledge for his 'aqiqah, sacrificed on the seventh day, his head shaved, and he is named)
